title: A Verdict for the Witness
premise: Elodie Crane, the coroner of salt-bitten Marrow Bay, has quietly solved three deaths the police ruled accidents, guided by a ledger of debts hidden in the town's tide tables. When a drowned man washes up wearing clothes stolen from her own closet, she realizes someone is staging her as either killer or next victim. The trail leads to the Harrow family, whose shipping fortune was built on a decades-old wreck they caused and covered up — and to Thomas Vane, the witness who survived it and has been sending Elodie coded warnings for years. In the climax, Elodie decodes the final ledger entry at low tide, exposing the Harrows' patriarch, but only after Thomas sacrifices his anonymity to save her from being made the fourth 'accident.' The book ends with Elodie choosing to stay in Marrow Bay, no longer hiding behind her dead, as the truth — and her love for Thomas — finally surfaces.
about_author: Quentin Dunmore is the pen name of a former maritime insurance investigator who spent eleven years auditing claims along the Atlantic coast before turning to fiction. He writes mysteries about small towns where everyone knows the water keeps secrets — until it doesn't.

chapters.title: Every Grave by Name
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. She performs a routine autopsy on an elderly fisherman and notes injuries inconsistent with the police's 'fall' ruling — the third such case this year. We learn her habit of speaking to the dead and her isolation in Marrow Bay. Emotional beat: quiet competence masking loneliness; she trusts corpses more than the living.

chapters.title: The Tide Tables
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Cross-referencing the three deaths against old harbor records, she finds each victim's name penciled beside a date in a battered tide table book kept in the morgue. Someone has been keeping a ledger of deaths. Emotional beat: the thrill of pattern recognition curdling into dread that the ledger is still being written.

chapters.title: A Stranger Wearing Her Coat
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. A body washes up at Gull Point dressed in clothes stolen from her own closet, down to her father's watch. Sheriff Dane Rook dismisses her alarm; the clothes prove nothing, he says. Emotional beat: violation and fear — whoever did this knows her intimately and wants her implicated or targeted.

chapters.title: Sheriff Rook's Patience
chapters.summary: Rook's POV. The sheriff investigates Elodie half-heartedly, more interested in protecting the town's image than finding truth. Flashbacks reveal he buried one of her earlier findings under pressure from above. Emotional beat: a decent man grown complicit through exhaustion; he warns her, almost kindly, to stop digging.

chapters.title: The Man Who Watches the Water
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. She notices a gaunt man photographing the shoreline near where the body surfaced; he vanishes when approached but leaves behind a note in cipher tucked under a mooring cleat. Emotional beat: wary curiosity — the first sign she has an ally who communicates like she does, in things left unsaid.

chapters.title: Harrow House
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Following the ledger's oldest entries, she visits the Harrow estate, where matriarch Vivienne Harrow receives her with velvet menace and mentions the drowned man by name before it's public. Emotional beat: the chill of realizing wealth in Marrow Bay means immunity, and Vivienne knows exactly what Elodie has found.

chapters.title: What the Wreck Took
chapters.summary: Thomas Vane's POV (unnamed to Elodie). The watcher is revealed: sole survivor of the 1989 Corinne Mae sinking, which the Harrows caused by overloading the boat to hide smuggling losses. He has spent thirty years documenting debts owed to the drowned. Emotional beat: guilt of survival — he lived because he jumped first.

chapters.title: Cipher in the Margins
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Decoding the note using the tide-table ledger as a key, she finds coordinates and a warning: 'He wears your coat so they will bury you instead of me.' Emotional beat: terror sharpening into resolve; the staged body was meant to redirect the Harrows' attention onto her.

chapters.title: An Accident, Properly Arranged
chapters.summary: Rook's POV. Under orders from county officials tied to Harrow money, Rook is pressured to rule the drowned man's death accidental and open a file on Elodie. He stalls, torn. Emotional beat: the price of survival paid in small surrenders; Rook begins secretly feeding Elodie case details.

chapters.title: The Fourth Name
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. A fresh entry appears in the tide-table ledger in unfamiliar handwriting: her own name, dated three days out. She realizes the killer uses the morgue itself. Emotional beat: hunted in her own sanctuary; she stops sleeping and starts setting traps.

chapters.title: Low Tide Confessions
chapters.summary: Thomas and Elodie meet properly on the exposed flats at low tide. He reveals the Corinne Mae truth and the full ledger: every death since 1989 that closed a Harrow liability. Emotional beat: two lonely keepers of the dead recognizing each other; the first warmth either has allowed in years.

chapters.title: Vivienne's Ledger
chapters.summary: Vivienne's POV. The matriarch, dying, reflects on forty years of payments, threats, and drownings done mostly by her late husband and now by her son Aldous, whom she can no longer control. Emotional beat: love against duty inverted — she protected the family name at the cost of her soul and now cannot stop what she built.

chapters.title: Aldous Harrow's Clean Hands
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. She confronts Aldous at his marina office; he is charming, alibied, and unmistakably the hand behind the staged body. He offers her a bribe framed as a research grant. Emotional beat: seduction of complicity — the easy life offered to a woman tired of being poor and unheard.

chapters.title: The Witness File
chapters.summary: Rook's POV. Rook discovers the original 1989 investigation was closed by his predecessor on Harrow money, and that Thomas Vane was declared dead in absentia to erase him. He copies the file. Emotional beat: a lawman choosing, at last, which side of the ledger he stands on.

chapters.title: Burned
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Her cottage is ransacked; the tide-table ledger is stolen, and a fire is set to look like her own carelessness. She escapes with the decoded pages sewn into her coat lining. Emotional beat: loss of home and history — the price of survival is everything you can't carry.

chapters.title: Ghosts in the Harbor Office
chapters.summary: Thomas's POV. Thomas breaks into the Harrow shipping archives and photographs the falsified manifests, but trips a silent alarm. He escapes wounded, leaving blood on the dock. Emotional beat: the survivor finally risking the life he hoarded, knowing exposure may cost him everything.

chapters.title: The Trap at Gull Point
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Using the ledger dates, Elodie predicts the next staged death will be staged at Gull Point during the spring tide — with her as the corpse. She and Rook set a counter-trap. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into agency; the hunted becomes the hunter.

chapters.title: Spring Tide
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging. Aldous arrives to stage Elodie's drowning; Rook moves in; Vivienne, having learned her son intends to kill the coroner publicly, sends an anonymous tip that brings the whole town's boats to the point. Emotional beat: collision — every secret converges on one stretch of water.

chapters.title: What the Water Gives Back
chapters.summary: Climax. Aldous, cornered, tries to drown Elodie among the pilings; Thomas reveals himself publicly to pull Aldous off, taking a beating that ends when Rook arrests Aldous with the archive photos and ledger as evidence. Emotional beat: love against duty fulfilled — Thomas trades his invisibility, the thing that kept him alive, for Elodie's life.

chapters.title: Verdicts
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Inquests reopen; the three 'accidents' and the Corinne Mae nine are formally reclassified. Vivienne, testifying from a wheelchair, confesses to the cover-up to bury her son's chances of walking free. Emotional beat: justice arriving too late for the dead but not too late for the living; grief with somewhere to go.

chapters.title: Names Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. At a memorial on the flats, Elodie reads the names of all the ledger's dead aloud as the tide comes in, and the town — complicit and grieving — listens. Thomas stands beside her, named at last. Emotional beat: belonging earned through truth; the community absorbing its own guilt.

chapters.title: A Verdict for the Witness
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Elodie's POV. Months later, Elodie buries the last unclaimed Corinne Mae victim and closes the tide-table ledger for good. Thomas asks if she'll leave Marrow Bay now that the secrets are spent; she says the dead here are hers. Emotional beat: peace chosen deliberately — love rooted in the place that nearly killed them both.
